findings.message: <div data-composition-id="t3-prompt-send" data-start="0" data-track-index="1"> has no id, so Studio cannot use a stable edit target for its timeline and canvas controls.
findings.selector: [data-composition-id="t3-prompt-send"]
findings.fixHint: Add a stable, human-readable id such as id="hero-title" or id="scene-1-card" to every timeline-visible element you want agents or Studio to edit.

findings.message: This composition has 80 elements carrying "heavy overlay" CSS (filter:blur, radial-gradient, or clip-path). Field signal: a composition with ~40 such elements — including opacity:0 / visibility:hidden ones — captures solid-black for the first ~half of the render, recovering near the end. Reproduces identically via drawElement, forced screenshot capture, and snapshot, so the capture layer itself is the offender (not encoder/mux). Independent of duration. Presence alone matters; only display:none elements are excluded here.
findings.selector: [data-composition-id]
findings.fixHint: Split this sub-composition further into per-transition mini-compositions and concat the pieces (FFmpeg or the runtime's slideshow) so each capture only sees a small subset of heavy overlays at once. Even hidden overlays (opacity:0 / visibility:hidden) contribute — either remove truly unused ones from the source or scope them into their own per-transition sub-composition. If an overlay is genuinely inert for the whole clip, use display:none so it never enters the render tree. Field ref ts=1784040753 (#hyperframes-cli-feedback).
